objects.name: Sagittarius A*
objects.facts: The 4.3-million-solar-mass black hole at the centre of the Milky Way; imaged by the Event Horizon Telescope in 2022.

objects.name: M87* (Pōwehi)
objects.facts: A 6.5-billion-solar-mass black hole in galaxy M87 — the first black hole ever directly imaged (EHT, 2019).

objects.name: TON 618
objects.facts: One of the most massive black holes known (~66 billion M☉), powering a hyperluminous quasar.

objects.name: Phoenix A
objects.facts: A candidate for the most massive black hole known (~100 billion M☉) at the heart of the Phoenix Cluster.

objects.name: OJ 287 primary
objects.facts: A blazar hosting an ~18-billion-solar-mass black hole orbited by a smaller one — a natural black-hole binary.

objects.name: NGC 1277 BH
objects.facts: A 'relic' galaxy whose black hole is startlingly massive for the galaxy's size.

objects.name: Cygnus X-1
objects.facts: The first widely accepted black hole (1971); ~21 M☉, feeding on a blue-supergiant companion.

objects.name: Gaia BH1
objects.facts: The closest known black hole to Earth (2022), ~10 M☉ orbited by a Sun-like star.

objects.name: V404 Cygni
objects.facts: A black-hole binary that dramatically flared in 2015; ~9 M☉.

objects.name: GRO J1655-40
objects.facts: A black hole ejecting jets at ~92% the speed of light.

objects.name: A0620-00
objects.facts: One of the nearest black holes to Earth, ~6.6 M☉.

objects.name: LMC X-1
objects.facts: A black hole in the Large Magellanic Cloud.

objects.name: Crab Pulsar
objects.facts: A neutron star spinning 30 times a second — the collapsed core of the SN 1054 supernova.

objects.name: Vela Pulsar
objects.facts: A nearby young pulsar and gamma-ray source in the Vela supernova remnant.

objects.name: PSR B1919+21
objects.facts: The first pulsar ever detected (1967) — briefly nicknamed 'LGM-1'.

objects.name: PSR J0740+6620
objects.facts: One of the most massive neutron stars known (~2.1 M☉), a key test of ultra-dense matter.

objects.name: PSR B1257+12
objects.facts: Host of the first confirmed exoplanets (1992) — worlds orbiting a dead star.

objects.name: SGR 1806-20
objects.facts: A magnetar whose 2004 giant flare was the brightest extrasolar event ever recorded in gamma rays.

objects.name: Geminga
objects.facts: A radio-quiet gamma-ray pulsar, one of the closest to Earth.

objects.name: Crab Nebula (M1)
objects.facts: The expanding wreckage of a star seen to explode in 1054 AD, recorded by Chinese astronomers.

objects.name: Tycho's SNR (SN 1572)
objects.facts: Remnant of the 1572 supernova that helped overturn belief in unchanging heavens.

objects.name: Kepler's SNR (SN 1604)
objects.facts: The last naked-eye supernova seen in the Milky Way, observed by Kepler in 1604.

objects.name: Cassiopeia A
objects.facts: The youngest known Milky-Way remnant (~350 yr) and the brightest radio source in the sky.

objects.name: Vela SNR
objects.facts: A large, nearby remnant ~11,000 years old, home to the Vela Pulsar.

objects.name: SN 1987A
objects.facts: The nearest observed supernova in modern times (LMC) — the first with detected neutrinos.

objects.name: Veil Nebula (Cygnus Loop)
objects.facts: A delicate, filamentary remnant 10,000–20,000 years old.

objects.name: Orion Nebula (M42)
objects.facts: The nearest large star-forming region, visible to the naked eye in Orion's sword.

objects.name: Eagle Nebula (M16)
objects.facts: Home of the 'Pillars of Creation', columns of gas birthing new stars.

objects.name: Carina Nebula
objects.facts: A vast star-forming region hosting the volatile hypergiant Eta Carinae.

objects.name: Ring Nebula (M57)
objects.facts: A dying Sun-like star's shed outer layers, glowing as a smoke ring.

objects.name: Helix Nebula
objects.facts: One of the nearest planetary nebulae, the 'Eye of God'.

objects.name: Lagoon Nebula (M8)
objects.facts: A giant interstellar cloud and star-forming region in Sagittarius.

objects.name: Cat's Eye Nebula
objects.facts: An intricately structured planetary nebula.

objects.name: Horsehead Nebula
objects.facts: A dark cloud of dust silhouetted against glowing gas in Orion.

objects.name: Rosette Nebula
objects.facts: A rose-shaped cloud with a young star cluster at its heart.

objects.name: TRAPPIST-1
objects.facts: A cool dwarf with seven Earth-sized planets, three in the habitable zone.

objects.name: Proxima Centauri b
objects.facts: The closest exoplanet — a roughly Earth-mass world in the habitable zone of the nearest star.

objects.name: 51 Pegasi (Dimidium)
objects.type: first exoplanet at a Sun-like star
objects.facts: The 1995 discovery of 51 Peg b launched the exoplanet era (Nobel Prize 2019).

objects.name: Kepler-90
objects.facts: A system with eight known planets, matching our Solar System's count.

objects.name: Kepler-452
objects.facts: Host of Kepler-452b, an Earth-size planet in a Sun-like star's habitable zone.

objects.name: HD 209458 (Osiris)
objects.facts: The first exoplanet seen to transit its star and the first with a detected atmosphere.

objects.name: TOI-700
objects.facts: A red dwarf with an Earth-size planet, TOI-700 d, in the habitable zone.

objects.name: 55 Cancri
objects.facts: Includes 55 Cancri e, a scorching 'super-Earth' possibly rich in carbon.

objects.name: HR 8799
objects.facts: One of the first systems whose planets were seen directly in images — four giant worlds around a young star.

objects.name: K2-18
objects.facts: A super-Earth/sub-Neptune whose atmosphere shows water vapour and carbon-bearing molecules.

objects.name: LHS 1140
objects.facts: A quiet red dwarf hosting a dense rocky planet, LHS 1140 b, in its habitable zone.

objects.name: GJ 1214
objects.facts: Host of a much-studied sub-Neptune with a thick, steamy atmosphere.

objects.name: Gliese 667 C
objects.facts: A red dwarf in a triple system with several planets, some near the habitable zone.

objects.name: Kepler-16
objects.facts: A planet orbiting two stars at once — the first confirmed circumbinary world.

objects.name: PSR B1257+12
objects.facts: A pulsar whose planets (1992) were the first exoplanets ever confirmed.

objects.name: WASP-12
objects.facts: A gas giant so close to its star it is being tidally shredded and devoured.

objects.name: Gliese 486
objects.facts: A nearby transiting rocky super-Earth, a prime target for atmospheric study.

objects.name: TOI-1452
objects.facts: A super-Earth possibly covered by a deep global ocean.

objects.name: Alpha Centauri
objects.facts: The Sun's nearest neighbours — a Sun-like pair (Rigil Kentaurus & Toliman) plus the red dwarf Proxima; humanity's first interstellar target.

objects.name: Barnard's Star
objects.facts: A red dwarf with the largest known proper motion, drifting a Moon-width across the sky each 180 years.

objects.name: Sirius
objects.facts: The brightest star in the night sky — a hot A-type star with a white-dwarf companion, Sirius B.

objects.name: Luhman 16
objects.facts: A pair of brown dwarfs; the third-closest system to the Sun.

objects.name: Wolf 359
objects.facts: A faint, active red dwarf; one of the closest stars and a science-fiction landmark.

objects.name: Epsilon Eridani
objects.facts: A young Sun-like star with a dusty debris disk and a giant planet — a nearby analogue of the early Solar System.

objects.name: Tau Ceti
objects.facts: The closest solitary star resembling the Sun; a long-standing target in the search for other Earths.

objects.name: Procyon
objects.facts: The eighth-brightest star, an F-type subgiant with a white-dwarf companion, Procyon B.

objects.name: Vega
objects.facts: A brilliant nearby A-type star with a dusty debris disk; a former and future northern pole star.

objects.name: Fomalhaut
objects.facts: A young star girdled by a sharp dust ring — the "Eye of Sauron" — sculpted by unseen bodies.

objects.name: 40 Eridani (Keid)
objects.facts: A nearby triple with a white dwarf and red dwarf; fictionally the home of Star Trek's Vulcan.

objects.name: Altair
objects.facts: A brilliant, rapidly spinning A-type star flattened into an oblate spheroid by its own spin.

objects.name: M87 (Virgo A)
objects.facts: A giant elliptical firing a 5,000-light-year plasma jet; hosts the first-imaged black hole.

objects.name: Whirlpool Galaxy (M51)
objects.facts: A classic face-on spiral interacting with a small companion galaxy.

objects.name: Sombrero Galaxy (M104)
objects.facts: An edge-on spiral with a bright bulge and a striking dark dust lane.

objects.name: Cartwheel Galaxy
objects.facts: A ring galaxy sculpted by a head-on collision.

objects.name: Antennae Galaxies
objects.facts: Two galaxies caught mid-collision, triggering intense bursts of star formation.

objects.name: Messier 77
objects.facts: A prototype Seyfert galaxy with an actively feeding central black hole.

objects.name: Pinwheel Galaxy (M101)
objects.facts: A large, face-on grand-design spiral galaxy.

objects.name: 3C 273
objects.facts: The first object recognised as a quasar (1963) and the optically brightest in our sky.

objects.name: 3C 279
objects.facts: A blazar showing apparent superluminal jet motion.

objects.name: ULAS J1342+0928
objects.facts: One of the most distant quasars, seen ~690 million years after the Big Bang.

objects.name: Markarian 421
objects.facts: One of the closest, best-studied blazars and a TeV gamma-ray source.

objects.name: APM 08279+5255
objects.facts: An extremely luminous, gravitationally lensed quasar.

objects.name: BL Lacertae
objects.facts: The prototype of the 'BL Lac' class of blazars.

objects.name: GW150914
objects.facts: The first direct detection of gravitational waves (2015): two black holes (~36 & 29 M☉) merging. (Position approximate.)

objects.name: GW170817
objects.facts: The first neutron-star merger seen in both gravitational waves and light — a forge of heavy elements like gold.

objects.name: GRB 221009A
objects.facts: The 'brightest of all time' gamma-ray burst (2022), from a collapsing massive star.

objects.name: GRB 080319B
objects.facts: A gamma-ray burst briefly visible to the naked eye despite its immense distance.

objects.name: FRB 121102
objects.facts: The first fast radio burst found to repeat, localized to a distant dwarf galaxy.

objects.name: UY Scuti
objects.facts: Among the largest known stars — placed at the Sun it would reach beyond Jupiter's orbit.

objects.name: VY Canis Majoris
objects.facts: A colossal, unstable red hypergiant shedding vast amounts of mass.

objects.name: Eta Carinae
objects.facts: A ~100-solar-mass unstable pair that erupted in the 1840s and may soon go supernova.

objects.name: R136a1
objects.facts: The most massive star known (~200 M☉), in the Tarantula Nebula of the LMC.

objects.name: Betelgeuse
objects.facts: A doomed red supergiant that will one day explode as a brilliant supernova.

objects.name: WR 104
objects.facts: A Wolf-Rayet star spinning out a spiral 'pinwheel' of dust.

objects.name: Stephenson 2-18
objects.facts: A candidate for the largest known star by radius.
